papers.title: Nucleus reuniens gates selective hippocampal-prefrontal interactions during NREM sleep
papers.summary: Using in vivo electrophysiology in rats during NREM sleep, the authors identified ripple-like activity in nucleus reuniens (~120 Hz, ~45 ms) that phase-locked to hippocampal sharp wave-ripples and mPFC ripples and was associated with thalamic spiking. HC-mPFC ripple coupling mainly occurred with co-occurring RE ripples, suggesting RE ripples gate hippocampal-prefrontal interactions during sleep.

papers.title: Mouse bio-behavioral phenotyping using a digital homecage framework for long-timescale, high-resolution, and multi-factor data collection and analytics.
papers.summary: The authors present the Digital Homecage (DHC), an open-source platform for continuous long-term monitoring of over 20 behavioral metrics in single-housed mice using video, operant tasks, and wheel-running. Initial data validated its ability to capture circadian patterns across spontaneous behaviors, consistently reflecting nocturnal activity.

papers.title: Repeated self-administered EEG recordings enable longitudinal measurement of brain activity at home
papers.summary: Five participants completed repeated self-administered at-home EEG sessions (resting state and auditory oddball with/without cognitive load) using a four-channel consumer device and captured expected alpha, theta, and event-related response signatures. Aggregating sessions improved reliability, with split-half reliability of the N1-like response rising from r = .22 for one session to r = .76 for seven sessions per half.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.summary: This high-definition review evaluates evidence that acupuncture modulates sleep microarchitecture (EEG spectral power, spindles, slow oscillations), finding that direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is very limited and mainly indirect from wake or anesthesia studies. It distinguishes observed findings from hypotheses and outlines pathways and future research requirements.

papers.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity.
papers.summary: Drosophila antimicrobial peptide (AMP) mutants were characterized for sleep and plasticity, showing reduced sleep, longer sleep latency, and altered arousal thresholds, with the double Mtk/Drs (Group C) mutant most impaired and exhibiting exaggerated sleep rebound. Group C mutants retained normal learning and memory despite sleeping least and had lower synapse abundance, while other AMP mutants showed sleep and memory deficits that were reversible with sleep enhancement.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.summary: The study applied a pre-registered three-criterion validation framework to 18 EEG features across three independent cohorts to screen candidate amyotrophic lateral sclerosis biomarkers. Gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy met all three criteria (cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, cross-cohort effect consistency), and permutation testing found no permuted three-cohort reliability intersection (Monte Carlo p = 0.001), though bootstrap resampling showed sensitivity of the selected set to sample composition.

papers.title: Regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences exceed longitudinal changes across an approximately 34-h protocol: a prospective quality-controlled proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
papers.summary: In a prospective quality-controlled 1H-MRS study of 138 participants scanned about 34 h apart, regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences were larger and more robust than longitudinal changes, with a median absolute paired standardized effect size of 0.571 for region versus 0.125 for longitudinal change. PCC showed higher NAA/Cr and SVS GlxT/Cr, while ACC showed higher Cho/Cr and MEGA Glu/Cr; follow-up reductions surviving FDR correction were confined to SVS Cr2/Cr and GlxT/Cr.

papers.title: Light-induced melatonin suppression in school-aged children before and during camping: associations with circadian phase and daytime light exposure
papers.summary: In 21 school-aged children, evening light-induced melatonin suppression did not differ significantly before versus after roughly two weeks of natural light-dark cycle exposure during camp (p = 0.21). Greater suppression was associated with later DLMO pre-camp (rho = 0.49) and with lower same-day daytime illuminance during camp (rho = -0.58), indicating large interindividual variation linked to circadian phase and recent light exposure.

papers.title: Altered heart-brain coupling in awake patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.summary: Using whole-night polysomnography, this study compared heartbeat evoked potentials (HEPs) across wakefulness, NREM, and REM sleep in 13 patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder and 23 healthy controls. Patients showed altered frontal HEPs during wakefulness between 305 and 445 ms after the R-peak, with no significant differences during NREM or REM and no explanation by ECG differences, suggesting a potential waking quantitative biomarker for iRBD.

papers.title: Chronic buprenorphine-associated severe central sleep apnea and desaturation proof of concept.
papers.summary: This retrospective polysomnographic study of 11 chronic buprenorphine users identified two breathing patterns: four patients with central sleep apnea (mean central apnea index 13/h, AHI 35/h, nadir saturation 75%) and seven without significant CSA who nonetheless had prolonged desaturation below 90% (91 vs 51 min), suggesting hypoventilation. It provides preliminary evidence that chronic buprenorphine is associated with clinically significant sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: This uncontrolled pilot study compared resting-state EEG in 6–8-year-old children with autism spectrum disorder (n=20) and typically developing children (n=15), and examined pre-post changes around a single 30-min Berard auditory integration training session using FOOOF spectral parameterization. At baseline, ASD showed higher delta and lower theta, alpha, and beta relative power; post-session, delta decreased and beta/gamma increased, while aperiodic exponent and offset showed no significant changes.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform and machine-learning framework using single-channel EEG features (approximate entropy, rhythm energy ratio, C0-complexity, zero-crossing rate) with representative channel selection. Under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, Decision Tree classifiers achieved accuracies of 84.52% (F4) for schizophrenia, 86.54% (F4) for Parkinson's disease, and 93.10% (Fp1) for depression.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Intensive Continuous Theta Burst Stimulation Over the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Insomnia Disorder:A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial gave 30 adults with insomnia disorder 21 sessions of continuous theta burst stimulation over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex or sham cTBS, with both groups improving on all sleep outcomes without significant group×time interactions. Active cTBS produced a significant, large advantage in health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF, P=.002, ηp2=0.242) and was safe and well tolerated.

papers.title: Sub-Threshold Stochastic Vibration Improves Fingertip Tactile Sensitivity in Stroke Survivors and Healthy Adults, with Source-Localized EEG Evidence for Cortical Network Reorganization in Healthy Adults
papers.summary: In 19 healthy adults and 5 stroke survivors, adding sub-threshold stochastic vibration lowered 30 Hz sinusoidal fingertip detection thresholds in every participant, with sensitivity gains up to 19-fold in healthy adults and up to 4-fold in stroke survivors. Source-localized high-density EEG in healthy participants showed increased functional connectivity, most extensively in the alpha band with frontal involvement, while super-threshold noise produced weaker beta-band changes consistent with masking rather than resonance.

papers.title: Robust Feature Engineering Techniques for Designing Efficient Motor Imagery-Based Systems Using Multidomain Electroencephalography
papers.summary: Engineered multidomain EEG features (time, frequency, wavelet; 416 total) from the MILimbEEG dataset and applied MRMR to select four features, yielding Gaussian-kernel SVM test accuracies of 92.50% for motor activities and 95.48% for motor imagery. Shows that strong motor imagery classification can be retained with a drastically reduced feature set.

papers.title: Effects of heart rate variability biofeedback and relaxation training on ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity in young patients with depressive disorders: An EEG study.
papers.summary: Compared 5-week heart rate variability biofeedback versus relaxation training on EEG current source density in bilateral vmPFC of 45 young patients with depressive disorder. HRVB showed greater right vmPFC beta3 and left vmPFC high-beta CSD during transfer versus RT, while both groups showed increased theta CSD, suggesting shared relaxation effects plus HRVB-specific vmPFC engagement.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG during a dot-perspective task, this study compared neural generators of altercentric and egocentric biases in healthy controls (n=24) and forensic BPD patients (n=14). In BPD, no significant differential activation was observed, suggesting decreased ability to mobilize brain resources for self-other discrepancy, though limited power requires confirmation.

papers.title: Cortical Network Alterations and Treatment-Induced Reorganization in Panic Disorder: A Longitudinal High-Density EEG Study.
papers.summary: Used 128-channel resting-state high-density EEG in 52 drug-naive panic disorder patients and 43 controls, plus 6-week venlafaxine follow-up, to characterize source-level functional connectivity and network topology. Baseline alpha-band hyperconnectivity and reduced theta/delta connectivity distinguished groups (SVM accuracy 86.32%), and treatment was accompanied by increased alpha global efficiency and small-worldness and enhanced delta fronto-temporal connectivity.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: clinical assessment, treatable syndromes, and limits of biomarker inference.
papers.summary: This narrative review links sleep and circadian assessment in Alzheimer's disease to indication-based care, distinguishing symptomatic benefit, physiological target engagement, and disease modification. It covers actigraphy, melatonin timing and temperature rhythms, polysomnography, and quantitative EEG, and organizes clinical priorities such as obstructive sleep apnea, cognition-adapted insomnia care, irregular sleep timing, and excessive daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.summary: This dual between-groups and within-subjects EEG study compared long-term Tibetan Buddhist practitioners of Tantra (n=21) and Sutra (n=20) meditation in monastery settings. The Tantra group showed consistently lower alpha power across meditation and baseline conditions, and only the Tantra group showed increased individual alpha peak frequency in occipital leads during meditation, followed by a decrease afterward.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances in Female Military Personnel: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review screened 6,839 records and included 19 studies on sleep disturbances in female military personnel, finding greater vulnerability to insomnia onset, recurrence, and physiological dysregulation compared with male personnel. It identified 11 multilayered biological, psychological, socio-environmental, and structural risk factors and calls for tailored sleep hygiene interventions.

papers.title: Association of Self-Reported Sleep and Circadian Variability and Moral Judgements and Decision-Making.
papers.summary: Observational online survey of 109 healthy adults (18–39 years) examined associations of self-reported sleep and circadian factors with moral and social judgements. Greater online vigilantism and aversion to causing/witnessing harm were associated with earlier chronotype, higher sleep regularity, and less social jetlag (r > 0.20), while dictator-game generosity showed no significant association.

papers.title: Quantitative effects of sleep deprivation on digital pupillary dynamics and visual evoked potential metrics in healthy adults.
papers.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health
papers.summary: In 18 healthy adults under controlled 48-hour sleep deprivation, pupillary light reflex dilation-phase parameters (DDil1, DDil2) and the VEP N145 component latency/amplitude were identified as sensitive biomarkers of fatigue, corroborated by the pupillary sleepiness test and Stanford Sleepiness Scale. The dilation-phase measures complemented established fatigue indices such as constriction velocity and relative amplitude.

papers.title: Pharmacotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence through June 2026 on pharmacotherapy for the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD—major depressive disorder, sleep disturbances including insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea, alcohol use disorders, and psychoses—and concludes that medication choice must be highly individualized because agents used for PTSD largely do not treat comorbid symptoms.

papers.title: A volumetric threshold and age-dependent remodeling are associated with residual obstructive sleep apnea after adenotonsillectomy in children.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 238 children with OSA undergoing adenotonsillectomy, postoperative upper-airway volume below 10.5 cm³ (AUC=0.89) and younger age independently predicted residual OSA. Complete resolution occurred in 63.4%, and age-dependent soft-tissue remodeling was implicated in persistent disease.

papers.title: Prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation combined with cognitive training reduces anxiety, daytime sleepiness, and cognitive complaints in women after COVID-19: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of 30 women with post-COVID cognitive complaints, adding left dorsolateral prefrontal tDCS (2 mA, 9 sessions) to cognitive training reduced anxiety and daytime sleepiness and improved global cognition, memory, fluency, and psychomotor speed versus both CT+sham and CT-only groups, with parallel increases in prefrontal cortical arousal and a shift toward left-frontal activation.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration and sleep-timing patterns with depressive mood and suicidal outcomes in Korean adolescents.
papers.summary: Using nationally representative 2025 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey data from ~48,000 adolescents, this cross-sectional study found that weekly average sleep duration (nonlinearly, with higher odds at short durations) and the absolute weekday–weekend sleep midpoint difference were associated with depressive mood and all suicidal outcomes, whereas MSFsc associations were less robust and outcome-dependent.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: Retrospective Pediatric Health Information System cohort (2016–2025) of 13,202 neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation, examining institutional variation in EEG utilization and its association with outcomes. EEG monitoring occurred in 12.5% overall, rose from ~6% to >14% over time, and varied widely across hospitals (0% to >40%); EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection, longer length of stay, and higher hospitalization costs.

papers.title: Epidemiology, Complications, and Management of Complications of Achondroplasia: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic literature review and meta-analysis of 200 studies characterized the clinical burden of achondroplasia, reporting prevalence estimates from 1 to 67 per 100,000 births and common complications including sleep disordered breathing (mean 60%), cervicomedullary compression (mean 34%), and kyphosis (mean 43%). It highlights the high frequency and severity of complications and the need for effective treatments.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: clinical evidence and mechanistic perspectives.
papers.summary: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of four perioperative randomized trials (480 participants) found preliminary clinical signals that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation may reduce postoperative cognitive decline and delirium (delirium 12.0% vs 25.3%), while mechanistic evidence supports multilevel inflammatory, autonomic, and neurovascular pathways; certainty was low to very low.

papers.title: The combined effect of nighttime sleep duration and midday nap duration during pregnancy on full-term low birth weight: A case-control study.
papers.summary: In a hospital-based case-control study of 515 FT-LBW cases and 1030 controls, pregnant women with nighttime sleep <7.0 hours had a 100% higher risk of FT-LBW compared to those sleeping 7.0-9.0 hours (95% CI: 1.28-3.14). Longer midday nap duration was associated with lower FT-LBW risk (P for trend = .003), and the association between short nighttime sleep and FT-LBW was significant only in women who did not nap, indicating a synergistic effect.

papers.title: Sleep duration and risk of post-stroke depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 studies (5,624 cases) found that short sleep duration was associated with increased risk of post-stroke depression (OR 1.93, 95% CI 1.56–2.38), whereas long sleep duration was not significantly associated.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 11 studies found evidence suggesting an association between obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID, with proposed mechanisms including intermittent hypoxia, systemic inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, sleep fragmentation, and circadian disturbance, though the direction and causality remain uncertain and evidence on OSA treatment effects is limited.

papers.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence that Parkinson's disease is preceded by a reversible phase of dopaminergic hyperactivation (increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction) manifesting as early non-motor symptoms. Argues this pre-degenerative stage is detectable with multimodal biomarkers and targetable by calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory drugs acting on NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.summary: Open-label, single-arm exploratory trial in 19 patients with treatment-resistant depression receiving 6–12 sessions of 100-Hz magnetic seizure therapy targeting bilateral F3/F4, with clinical rating scales and 64-channel Go/Nogo task EEG before and after treatment. MST was associated with significant depressive symptom reduction (HAMD-24 40.53 to 22.53; response rates 42.1%–57.9%) and lower Nogo-related frontal theta activity at an uncorrected threshold, but EEG effects did not survive FDR correction and the uncontrolled design precludes mechanistic or biomarker conclusions.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian disruption as systemic drivers of breast cancer metastasis: A tri-pathway mechanistic model.
papers.summary: This review proposes a tri-pathway mechanistic model linking sleep deficiency and circadian disruption to breast cancer metastasis via melatonin suppression/neuroendocrine disruption, chronic inflammation with myeloid-derived suppressor cell expansion, and metabolic reprogramming, and discusses circadian biomarkers and chronobiology-based therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Integrative therapies for symptom management in dementia from a palliative perspective: narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.summary: Narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on integrative care therapies for dementia symptom management from a palliative perspective. Cognitive stimulation had the highest evidence certainty (high for communication and social interaction; moderate for cognition, quality of life, and challenging behaviors), music therapy showed moderate-certainty benefit for depression but not agitation, and most other modalities had low-to-very-low certainty evidence.

papers.title: The interplay of exercise, immunity, and suboptimal health in college students: an integrative narrative review with public health implications.
papers.summary: This integrative narrative review examines how different exercise types affect immune function, chronic low-grade inflammation, and suboptimal health status in college students, summarizing proposed mechanisms such as myokine-mediated anti-inflammatory signaling and immune cell mobilization while critiquing study-design and measurement limitations and offering public health implications.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sleep deprivation in nursing technicians working in shifts.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 198 nursing technicians at a Brazilian university hospital found a 43.9% prevalence of sleep deprivation (<5 hours/night). Associated factors included prolonged daily work hours (OR=3.60), anxiety symptoms (OR=6.58), coffee consumption (OR=3.14), inadequate fruit/vegetable intake (OR=2.25), and higher BMI (OR=1.27).

papers.title: Reversal of photoperiodic flowering in temperate grasses rewired light inputs and floral outputs of the circadian clock.
papers.summary: Using comparative transcriptomics and functional principal component analysis of diel gene expression in short-day-flowering Nassella pubiflora and long-day-flowering Oloptum miliaceum, this study found that the reversal from long-day to short-day flowering involved divergence in relatively few floral integrator, light-signalling, and circadian clock target genes rather than widespread changes to core clock gene expression.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
